No, it does not use a database transaction. According to [[write-journal]], the rollback mechanism "provides all-or-nothing semantics for writes without needing a database transaction; the journal itself acts as a transaction log held in process memory for the duration of one run."

So instead of a database transaction, it relies on an in-memory write journal that records the prior state of each file before it is overwritten, allowing the executor to restore previous content or delete newly created files in reverse order if needed.
